habitat: Pairs occur in broad-leaved woodland, thornveld and bush fringing dry riverbeds.
summary: A common resident, larger than Cardinal Woodpecker, with black streaks below. The male has a red malar streak and the whole crown is red with black spots. The female has a black crown with white spots and only the nape red. The call is a single nasal waaa. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and the tail colour were not described. The Kemp paper name Goldentailed Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cardinal Woodpecker is smaller, with a brown forehead. The male’s crown is crimson rather than red with black spots, and the female’s crown is black without a red nape.
Bennett’s Woodpecker is spotted below rather than streaked, and the female has brown patches on the face and throat.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. No month-by-month park calendar was published. Sexes differ on the crown and malar streak. The immature was not described. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and tail colour were not given. The straight bill and stiff tail are the family notes on the Newman page. No flight photograph was found. The Kruger frames are a female side from Mopani, a male front from the Pretoriuskop region, and a female back. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Goldentailed Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.
